Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Expectation2: Recite and reflect on the Quran
Situation2: A relaxed evening lies ahead with no other commitments.
Story: I had been looking forward to this evening all week—a rare stretch of quiet after days packed with work and errands. I’d planned to spend it reciting and reflecting on the Quran, something I’d been neglecting lately. The house was peaceful, the world outside dimming into dusk, and I felt a sense of calm settle over me as I opened the holy book. Just then, my phone buzzed, shattering the silence. It was Samir, his voice shaky and urgent. His car had broken down on the highway, miles from home, and he needed me to come get him right away. I could hear the anxiety in his voice, the expectation that I’d drop everything to help, as any good friend would. But as I glanced at the Quran in my lap, I felt torn. My heart ached with the weight of both responsibilities—my duty to my friend in his moment of need, and my longing to reconnect with my faith in the quiet I’d so carefully carved out. The two roles pulled at me, each demanding something I wasn’t sure I could give at the same time.
